subject.title: [BUG]: Browser tool: `snapshot` returns page content before scroll, ignoring viewport position

question: Should browser snapshot become visible-viewport scoped by default after scroll, or should OpenClaw preserve full-tree snapshot and add a separate visible-viewport read with scroll metadata?
rationale: The current implementation and docs intentionally expose a stable UI tree, while the requested behavior changes model-facing browser semantics and compatibility for workflows that rely on full-page reads.

options.title: Add Separate Visible Read
options.body: Preserve the existing full-tree snapshot contract and add a visible-viewport read or mode that returns scroll/viewport metadata and only the visible state.

options.title: Change Snapshot Default
options.body: Make snapshot itself visible-viewport scoped by default and require explicit full/raw options for full tree access, accepting the compatibility impact.

options.title: Defer To Browser API Umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open but track implementation under the broader browser API/state-signaling work if maintainers want one larger contract pass.

recommendation.title: Add Separate Visible Read
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing full-tree snapshot contract and add a visible-viewport read or mode that returns scroll/viewport metadata and only the visible state.

likelyOwner.reason: Browser snapshot semantics are a public tool/product contract, and history shows steipete as the strongest browser plugin product-surface contributor.
